name: Double-Hand Widget Selection (DHWS)
summary: The two-hand version of SHGWS: a cone around one hand's ray pre-selects candidates into a 2D list beside that hand, and the other hand's ray scrolls and picks the target in the list.
howItWorks: Pre-selection is identical to SHGWS: a cone around the dominant hand's ray outlines candidates and a held pinch opens a 2D widget near the hand listing them, closest to the ray first. Instead of finger scrolling and a wrist twist, the non-dominant hand points at the widget with a ray to scroll and select the item. It was built as an intermediate condition between raycasting and SHGWS; in a 27-participant Quest 3 study it had lower error rates and workload and higher usability than raycasting, and did not differ significantly from SHGWS.
advantages: Uses the familiar ray interaction to operate the widget.
Lower error rate than raycasting in dense scenes.

relationships.note: Bimanual variant built as a comparison condition.
Lower error rate than raycasting; time did not differ significantly.
Also a two-hand pick from a 2D interface.

review.notes: Coded from the SHGWS preprint, where it is a comparison condition. The paper says the other hand uses raycasting to scroll and select in the widget; the confirmation gesture is not stated, coded pinch as on the raycasting baseline.
